title.zh: 中性代际分布密度归约

summary: Reduce a (nvr, nvx, nx) neutral generation distribution to per-spatial-cell densities by the cylindrical quadrature sum of weight * distribution * dvx over both velocity axes, with the one-dimensional radial-weight projection path and uniform-column routing.

capability: Reduce a (nvr, nvx, nx) neutral generation distribution to per-spatial-cell densities by the cylindrical quadrature sum of weight * distribution * dvx over both velocity axes, with the one-dimensional radial-weight projection path and uniform-column routing.
operation: reduce a generation distribution to per-cell densities
one generation distribution plus cylindrical quadrature -> (nx,) densities
discovery.model: Discrete velocity-space density integral over the cylindrical quadrature
discovery.geometry: zero-dimensional spatial cells with a 2-D cylindrical velocity quadrature
discovery.boundary: distribution finite 3-D; weight finite nonnegative, one- or two-dimensional and aligned; dvx finite nonnegative aligned to the velocity axis

identity.relation: per-cell generation density: n[x] = sum over (vr, vx) of W(vr,vx) * f(vr,vx,x) * dvx[vx]
identity.direction: one generation distribution plus cylindrical quadrature -> (nx,) densities
identity.definition: With a full (nvr,nvx) weight the sum runs over both axes at once; with a one-dimensional radial weight the radial projection computes sum_r w[r] * (sum_x f[r,x,:]*dvx[x]); a full weight whose columns are all equal is routed to the radial path.
identity.model: Discrete velocity-space density integral over the cylindrical quadrature
identity.geometry: zero-dimensional spatial cells with a 2-D cylindrical velocity quadrature
identity.coordinates: distribution and weight in the source's discrete units, dvx in the axial cell measure; result in the source's discrete density unit
identity.boundary: distribution finite 3-D; weight finite nonnegative, one- or two-dimensional and aligned; dvx finite nonnegative aligned to the velocity axis
assumptions: The caller owns the cylindrical quadrature and its normalization; this asset integrates, it does not construct the quadrature.
The uniform-column routing is an exact algebraic identity of the two paths only in exact arithmetic; the float path is unchanged.

Declared finiteness tightening: the output is gated for finiteness, so extreme-but-valid inputs that would overflow fail closed rather than returning non-finite results, per the finite-output contract. The divergence is pinned by a bounded regression test.

inputs.name: cylindrical_weight
inputs.constraints: Finite and nonnegative; one-dimensional radial weights align to the radial axis, two-dimensional weights to the leading distribution axes.

inputs.name: dvx
inputs.constraints: Finite and nonnegative, aligned to the distribution's velocity axis.

outputs.name: density
outputs.constraints: Finite; signed values are preserved (no clamp).

preconditions: Aligned finite distribution and quadrature with nonnegative weights.
supported: Per-generation density reduction for atomic or molecular neutral fields on a shared quadrature.
excluded: Negative weights or cell sizes; misaligned axes: rejected.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for boolean, string or complex arrays; when the distribution is not three-dimensional, the weight is not one- or two-dimensional and aligned, dvx is not aligned, any field is non-finite, or any weight or cell size is negative.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError when the evaluation produces a non-finite result where the contract demands finiteness; no fallback is selected.
failure_semantics.partial_results: Never returned; a rejected call produces no result.

example.description: Reduce one random generation distribution with both weight forms and confirm the routing identity.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.kinetic import reduce_generation_density
f = np.ones((2, 2, 2))
w2 = np.full((2, 2), 0.5)
dx = np.array([0.5, 1.0])
result = reduce_generation_density(f, w2, dx)
np.testing.assert_allclose(result, [1.5, 1.5])
radial = np.array([0.25, 0.75])
uniform = np.repeat(radial[:, None], 2, axis=1)
np.testing.assert_array_equal(reduce_generation_density(f, uniform, dx), reduce_generation_density(f, radial, dx))
try:
    reduce_generation_density(f, np.ones((2, 2)), np.array([0.5, -1.0]))
except ValueError as error:
    assert 'aligned' in str(error)
else:
    raise AssertionError('a negative dvx must be rejected')
example.expected: Observed PASS: Per-cell densities matching the quadrature sum; the uniform-column routing identity holds; a negative dvx is rejected.

scope: That the two-dimensional-weight result equals the independent per-cell quadrature sum in the declared operation order.
That the one-dimensional radial weight reproduces the declared projection path.
That the uniform-column routing identity holds (two paths agree on column-uniform weights).
The alignment, real-input, nonnegativity and finite-output failure contracts.
